reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes creating StrongBlock nodes through a node-creation call to action tied to earning STRONG token rewards. Participation requires supplying 10 STRONG plus Ethereum, paying a recurring monthly fee, and accepting an approximately $2,600 node cost alongside a stated daily return, with NFT access and reward benefits also presented. The speaker qualifies that rewards are not guaranteed and may decrease, and the available video evidence does not establish actual rewards, transaction completion, or financial outcomes.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present the stated reward rate as a promise: he says it is “not guaranteed” and could fall. He also discloses the recurring cost of keeping a node active. Those qualifications matter when assessing whether a discussion of potential returns is deceptive. The video gives the audience a variable reward estimate and an ongoing expense, not a demonstrated net profit or a guaranteed outcome.

$15 monthly that you must pay each month for your node to keep going

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies an upfront token requirement, a monthly payment and a stated reward rate. But those figures alone do not establish that the rate is guaranteed or that the speaker conceals the cost. His explicit warning that the rate could decrease limits the inference the opening asks you to draw from the reward calculation.

citations.quote: you should have 10 strong to create. Simple, 10 strong plus ethereum to pay rents
point 10 is not guaranteed could become point 05

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualification does not change the video's central proposition. The speaker tells viewers they need 10 STRONG to create a node and describes recurring STRONG rewards for doing so. A return can be promoted without being guaranteed; acknowledging that its rate might fall does not turn this paid-node pitch into primarily market analysis.

opening.argument: Judge, the title promises a walkthrough of creating a node, and the speaker calls this a basic overview with further detail left for later. He walks through naming a node and connecting a wallet, then consults a block-count chart. That sequence supports reading the video as an operational demonstration: it shows what the interface requires and how the speaker understands the reward timing. A tutorial can discuss costs and rewards without establishing that anyone completed a transaction or received the projected return.

citations.quote: HOW TO CREATE A NODE IN 2 MINUTES
Today we will do a basic video and we will come back on subjects to show you how it works.
It will be connected to your wallet. there you see my wallet is there. You name your node

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the creation steps as a call to action. In context, those same steps are the subject of the promised tutorial. Its cost and reward figures explain what a viewer would encounter and how the system is presented; they do not, by themselves, show a completed purchase or an actual payout.

citations.quote: HOW TO CREATE A NODE IN 2 MINUTES
Someone who wants to create a node They will simply create a node by clicking here like that.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is also the means of promotion. The speaker tells viewers what tokens they need to create a node and describes a recurring reward for holding one. The chart does not verify a payout, but verification of a completed transaction is not necessary to recognize an instructional pitch for paid node returns.

citations.quote: So you just create a node by doing this, you should have 10 strong to create. Simple, 10 strong plus ethereum to pay rents, the fee is 14.95
You are rewarded 0.10 Strong every time that 7000 blocks block are created around ethereum

opening.argument: Judge, the described transaction has identifiable inputs and an ongoing service cost: 10 STRONG to create a node, Ethereum for fees, and a monthly payment to keep it operating. The speaker also describes nodes as delivering blockchain data. That is evidence of a paid service with a stated function, even if its economic merits remain uncertain. The cited material does not show a credential request, a recruitment requirement, a guaranteed return or a completed transfer to the speaker. The presence of a price and a reward claim should not substitute for evidence of those additional mechanisms.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening establishes what the speaker says participation costs and what it may pay. It does not establish that the described node fails to provide its stated function, that the speaker receives viewers' funds, or that viewers are promised an unchanging return. The monthly fee is presented as a cost of keeping the node operating, not concealed as a free route to income.

citations.quote: It delivers blockchain data, which are very important
$15 monthly that you must pay each month for your node to keep going
point 10 is not guaranteed could become point 05

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The speaker's account of what nodes do is not evidence that this purchase delivers the claimed service or returns. More importantly, the pitch explicitly links paying to create and maintain a node with receiving recurring STRONG rewards. A credential request or recruitment scheme is not required for that paid-return mechanism to be the video's focus.
